## Overview Enables quantized **Laguna** (`LagunaForCausalLM`) MoE inference on the Zen CPU backend. Laguna INT4 checkpoints mix grouped int4 and grouped int8 experts across their layers and route with ungrouped sigmoid scoring, neither of which the Zen CPU WNA16 path added in #54024 could handle, so the model previously could not load on it. This extends that path to grouped **W8A16** (DA8W8). ## Test Plan ```bash lm_eval --model vllm \ --model_args pretrained=$CKPT,dtype=bfloat16,max_model_len=4096 \ --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto \ --apply_chat_template --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=2048 ``` ```bash vllm bench throughput --model $CKPT --dtype bfloat16 \ --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 \ --num-prompts 256 --max-num-seqs <8|32> --max-model-len 2176 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching --seed 0 ``` Unit tests. tests/kernels/quantization/test_zen_da8w4.py and tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_fused_moe.py ## Test Result **Accuracy.** Laguna INT4 on AMD EPYC 9005 (Turin), 32 cores, bf16 activations, `VLLM_CPU_INT4_W4A8=1`. The checkpoint carries two compressed-tensors groups — `num_bits=4` over layers 1-30 and `num_bits=8` over layers 31-39, both `group_size=128`, symmetric, `strategy=group`. | Task | n-shot | Filter | Metric | Value | |---|---|---|---|---| | gsm8k | 5 | flexible-extract | exact_match | 0.9022 ± 0.0082 | | gsm8k | 5 | strict-match | exact_match | 0.8916 ± 0.0086 | **Throughput.** Same pod and build, 1024 in / 1024 out, 256 prompts. | max-num-seqs | Output tokens/s | |---|---| | 8 | 62.40 | | 32 | 116.74 | ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

> Thanks for the fix!
> 
> **Question**: What's the expected gsm8k score for Laguna?

Actually there isn't a published gsm8k number for Laguna to compare against, the released evals are mostly SWE-bench. We use gsm8k because it's the standard accuracy gate for vLLM CPU work and what we run internally.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Admitting MiniMax2 routing relies on process_weights_after_loading copying scoring_func and renormalize off the layer, but only the compressed-tensors method calls that hook. AutoGPTQMoEMethod._setup_kernel (auto_gptq.py:691) never does, and a sym GPTQ int4/int8 checkpoint maps to kInt4Static/kInt8Static, so it picks ZEN_CPU first. For a GPTQ checkpoint of Laguna or MiniMax-M2 on Zen with the default VLLM_CPU_INT4_W4A8=1, apply() then routes with softmax and renormalize=False, and the correction bias is ignored. On main this config failed at load because neither Zen nor CPUExpertsInt4 accepted MiniMax2; now it silently serves wrong output. I ran select_experts with these defaults against the layer's real config (64 random tokens, 128 experts, top-8): no token got the same expert set, and the weights summed to 0.30 instead of 1. Could you add the compressed-tensors hook call to AutoGPTQMoEMethod._setup_kernel, or derive these defaults from moe_config.routing_method so a missed hook can't fall back to softmax?

Nit: for a format _zen_cpu_num_bits doesn't recognise (e.g. a Quark checkpoint), this logs "unsupported weight width WNoneA16". VLLM_CPU_INT4_W4A8 now gates the int8 DA8W8 path too, but its doc (envs.py:921-922) and the message at :195 still say int4/DA8W4 only. With it set to 0, Laguna's int8 layers have no CPU backend left and the model fails to load.

nodes.body: Thanks for pointing this out. I've done as you've suggested and derived the defaults from moe_config.routing_method. Scoring and acceptance now read a single _ROUTING_SCORING table, so a routing method can't be admitted by _supports_routing_method unless apply() has an entry telling it how to score that method. It also fixes the correction bias you mentioned

Both wording issues fixed. An unreadable format now reports cannot read a weight width from <ConfigClass>.
The envs.py doc now reads "zentorch DA8W4 kernels for int4, and DA8W8 for grouped int8 MoE.
On the load failure with the flag set to 0: that one I'd like to leave as-is. As you've pointed out there's no W8A16 CPU MoE kernel for int8 to fall back to. The CPU backend is CPUExpertsInt4, which is int4-only. 
We do plan to add native (non-Zen) Laguna support, which is exactly the int8 gap in CPUExpertsInt4, so this should resolve as a follow-up rather than persist.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_bias", [False, True])
+def test_select_experts_sigmoid_scoring(with_bias):
+    """Ungrouped sigmoid routing, as MiniMax2 uses. A correction bias orders
+    the selection only; the weights come from the unbiased scores."""
+    set_random_seed(0)
+    num_tokens, expert_num, topk = 7, 16, 4
+    router_logits = torch.randn(num_tokens, expert_num)
+    bias = torch.randn(expert_num) if with_bias else None
+
+    topk_weights, topk_ids = select_experts(
+        hidden_states=torch.empty(num_tokens, 0),
+        router_logits=router_logits,
+        top_k=topk,
+        use_grouped_topk=False,
+        renormalize=True,
+        scoring_func="sigmoid",
+        e_score_correction_bias=bias,
+    )
+
+    scores = router_logits.float().sigmoid()
+    selection_scores = scores if bias is None else scores + bias
+    expected_ids = torch.topk(selection_scores, k=topk, dim=-1, sorted=False)[1]
+    expected_weights = scores.gather(1, expected_ids)
+    expected_weights = expected_weights / expected_weights.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+
+    assert topk_ids.dtype == torch.int32
+    order = topk_ids.argsort(dim=-1)
+    expected_order = expected_ids.argsort(dim=-1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        topk_ids.gather(1, order).to(torch.int64),
+        expected_ids.gather(1, expected_order),
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        topk_weights.gather(1, order), expected_weights.gather(1, expected_order)
+    )

inline_comments.body: Admitting MiniMax2 routing relies on process_weights_after_loading copying scoring_func and renormalize off the layer, but only the compressed-tensors method calls that hook. AutoGPTQMoEMethod._setup_kernel (auto_gptq.py:691) never does, and a sym GPTQ int4/int8 checkpoint maps to kInt4Static/kInt8Static, so it picks ZEN_CPU first. For a GPTQ checkpoint of Laguna or MiniMax-M2 on Zen with the default VLLM_CPU_INT4_W4A8=1, apply() then routes with softmax and renormalize=False, and the correction bias is ignored. On main this config failed at load because neither Zen nor CPUExpertsInt4 accepted MiniMax2; now it silently serves wrong output. I ran select_experts with these defaults against the layer's real config (64 random tokens, 128 experts, top-8): no token got the same expert set, and the weights summed to 0.30 instead of 1. Could you add the compressed-tensors hook call to AutoGPTQMoEMethod._setup_kernel, or derive these defaults from moe_config.routing_method so a missed hook can't fall back to softmax?

Nit: for a format _zen_cpu_num_bits doesn't recognise (e.g. a Quark checkpoint), this logs "unsupported weight width WNoneA16". VLLM_CPU_INT4_W4A8 now gates the int8 DA8W8 path too, but its doc (envs.py:921-922) and the message at :195 still say int4/DA8W4 only. With it set to 0, Laguna's int8 layers have no CPU backend left and the model fails to load.

inline_comments.body: Thanks for pointing this out. I've done as you've suggested and derived the defaults from moe_config.routing_method. Scoring and acceptance now read a single _ROUTING_SCORING table, so a routing method can't be admitted by _supports_routing_method unless apply() has an entry telling it how to score that method. It also fixes the correction bias you mentioned

Both wording issues fixed. An unreadable format now reports cannot read a weight width from <ConfigClass>.
The envs.py doc now reads "zentorch DA8W4 kernels for int4, and DA8W8 for grouped int8 MoE.
On the load failure with the flag set to 0: that one I'd like to leave as-is. As you've pointed out there's no W8A16 CPU MoE kernel for int8 to fall back to. The CPU backend is CPUExpertsInt4, which is int4-only. 
We do plan to add native (non-Zen) Laguna support, which is exactly the int8 gap in CPUExpertsInt4, so this should resolve as a follow-up rather than persist.

> Thanks for the fix!
> 
> **Question**: What's the expected gsm8k score for Laguna?

Actually there isn't a published gsm8k number for Laguna to compare against, the released evals are mostly SWE-bench. We use gsm8k because it's the standard accuracy gate for vLLM CPU work and what we run internally.
